name: Logic and proof
description: Statements, truth tables, arguments, direct and indirect proof, and induction, taught at the Kepler outpost.
about: Logic and proof realm: statements, truth tables, arguments and the proof methods, for an adult who has finished Foundations and nothing more. Same Kepler outpost; the airlock computers now follow written rules, and Mira has opened a Rules Hall to check every claim before anyone trusts it. The concept plan is docs/plans/LOGIC-PLAN.md.

chapters.name: Statements
chapters.blurb: True and false, not, and, or, if-then and if-and-only-if.

sector.name: Switch Room
sector.purpose: read every rule the airlock computer follows

sector.name: Control Panel
sector.purpose: check a rule against every case before we wire it in

chapters.name: Laws of logic
chapters.blurb: De Morgan’s laws, the contrapositive, quantifiers and counterexamples.

sector.name: Regulations Office
sector.purpose: rewrite every regulation without changing what it means

chapters.name: Arguments
chapters.blurb: Valid arguments, rules of inference, fallacies, nested quantifiers and knights and knaves.

sector.name: Council Chamber
sector.purpose: tell a sound argument from a merely persuasive one

chapters.name: Direct proof
chapters.blurb: Definitions, direct proof, proof by contrapositive and proof by cases.

sector.name: Proof Workshop
sector.purpose: show a rule holds for every number, not just the ones we tried

chapters.name: Indirect proof
chapters.blurb: Contradiction, counterexamples, existence, if-and-only-if proofs and flawed proofs.

sector.name: Inquiry Office
sector.purpose: settle a claim by ruling out every alternative

chapters.name: Induction
chapters.blurb: Mathematical induction for sums and inequalities, and strong induction.

sector.name: Long Stair
sector.purpose: prove a rule for every step of a stair that never ends

mentor.name: Mira
mentor.opening: I’m Mira. Every rule here makes a claim, and we have to {purpose}. Your task is “{title}.” {brief} The idea we need: {topic}.
mentor.closing: You already have everything this needs from Foundations. I’ll check the first table with you, and the guided steps are there whenever you want them.

copy.homeTitle:
Every rule makes a claim.
Learn to prove it.
copy.firstVisit: Welcome back. The outpost runs on written rules now, and some of them contradict each other. We start with one sentence and one question: is it true? Type 1 for true and 0 for false.
copy.allDone: You did it. Every rule in the hall is checked, and you can prove what holds for every number. Real analysis will use these tools to make limits exact, once you have finished Calculus 2.
copy.chaptersNote: Seven chapters. Learn every concept in a chapter to unlock a landmark for the outpost. Practice missions are optional.

skills.title: The skill tree
skills.text: Follow the prerequisite branches from statements to induction. Each mission you finish opens the ideas that are built on it.

visual.title: The truth table bench
visual.text: Pick any mission, change its statements and predict the table before you check it. Nothing here affects your progress, and it all works offline.

help.title: Every claim, checked.
help.intro: Logic starts where Foundations ends, with one sentence at a time. It teaches statements, truth tables, arguments and proof, and it ends with induction. Every new word and symbol is explained before you are asked to use it, with a worked example first.
help.answers: Truth values are typed as 1 for true and 0 for false. A proof is never typed in: the number it asks for is what you check.
